title: A City Simulator, Opened Up parameters
$comment: Every default below was read from the vendored micropolisJS source at commit f13a1624 and matches it exactly. A default that disagrees with the engine is the worst possible bug in this sandbox, because the sandbox exists to show what the engine's defaults are. Slider granularity is x-step, never multipleOf - see the note in bathtub's schema for why. Property order is the panel's reading order: in representation, which layer to watch (the simulation transport sits above it); in assumptions, the starting city, then the two rules the sandbox leads with, then the other rules, then the seed.

layer.title: Layer over the city
layer.description: One of the maps the simulation keeps, drawn over the city. "Follow the cycle" shows whichever map was updated last, and is meant for stepping through the cycle with the clock paused.

show_rail.title: Show all fifteen maps above the city

urban_form.title: Starting city
urban_form.description: Blocks is a downtown of full blocks with parks, thinning toward the edge, with shops along a main street and industry to the east. Grid is uniform bands of housing, shops and industry. Both are the same on every run. The parks and trees in blocks raise land value, so the two plans give different numbers under the same rules.

crime_base.title: Crime base
crime_base.description: The 128 in crime = 128 - land value + population density - police: the crime a place starts with before anything about it is counted. No data was used to set it.

crime_land_value_weight.title: Weight on land value
crime_land_value_weight.description: How much one point of land value lowers crime. The engine uses 1. At 0, land value has no effect on crime.

crime_police_weight.title: Weight on police
crime_police_weight.description: How much police coverage lowers crime. The engine uses 1. Coverage runs from 0 to 1,000 and crime from 0 to 250, so one station at full strength removes crime entirely.

land_value_centre_base.title: Land value at the center
land_value_centre_base.description: Land value at the city center, before distance is subtracted. The engine uses 34, which the code multiplies by 4, so the highest possible value is 136.

land_value_distance_divisor.title: Distance divisor
land_value_distance_divisor.description: The 2 in land value = 34 - distance from the city center / 2. A higher number makes land value fall more slowly with distance.

max_traffic_distance.title: How far traffic looks
max_traffic_distance.description: A zone counts as connected if a random walk along the roads reaches the kind of zone it needs within this many tiles: housing needs shops, shops need industry, industry needs housing. There are no routes or journey times.

smooth_passes.title: Police smoothing passes
smooth_passes.description: How many times the map of police stations is blurred to make police coverage. At 0, only the stations themselves are covered.

birth_rate.title: Birth rate
birth_rate.description: Growth of the residential population each turn, as a share of it. There are no ages, households or migration.

ext_market_index.title: Outside demand
ext_market_index.description: Demand for the city's industry from outside the city. In the game it is set by the difficulty level.

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: The starting number for the simulation's random choices. The same rules and the same starting city with a different seed give a different city.
